compared.difference: prop:reflexivity (statement 822-825, proof 827-829) counts the degenerate case in which a formula is derivable from a set that already contains it; its proof is a one-step appeal to the definition. Our candidate counts the transitivity step, which requires constructing a new derivation out of two given ones and re-justifying the hypothesis-dependent lines.

prop:monotonicity (statement 831-835, proof 837-840) counts the fact that adding hypotheses preserves derivability, which follows by leaving a derivation unchanged. Our candidate changes the derivation by substituting the second hypothesis and is not implied by monotonicity.
